_description: Task13 DRIFT field, COARSE transcription -- the 0.4mm far-field grid. The fine sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_fine.json) is the 0.1mm near-field and final grid. PAD/GAP SPLIT: this file uses pixelSize 3.6 / pixelGap 0.8 while the fine file uses 3.5 / 0.9. That is NOT a typo -- both are the same 4.4mm pitch, and each file uses the split that divides its OWN spacing exactly: 3.6/0.4=9 and 0.8/0.4=2 here, versus 3.5/0.1=35 and 0.9/0.1=9 there. The fine split cannot be used at the coarse spacing (3.5/0.4=8.75), which is the whole reason there are two files. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The drift length is 159.9 - 10.0 = 149.9mm, so 50 V/mm gives -50 * 149.9 = -7495 V. This file holds -7500, i.e. 50.03 V/mm nominal and 50.08 V/mm measured along the tile centre. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. GridPotential does NOT enter this calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field -- measured phi at the grid plane z=11.6mm is about -71 V, not GridPotential. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
